title: deferred-slo-prioritizer-and-regional-fallback-shim
author: Asha Verma
description:
Motivation: During recent regional congestion incidents we observed that long-tail low-priority requests could contribute to cascading latency spikes and SLO violations while higher-value requests starved. This PR introduces a deferred SLO prioritizer and a regional-safe fallback shim to improve graceful degradation without global capacity churn.

What this change does (high level): implements a small scheduling shim in the runtime request router that: 1) classifies incoming requests into priority bands (high/normal/deferred) using existing quota + client-provided hints; 2) defers execution of deferred-band requests for a short, bounded window (configurable, default 250ms) to allow higher-priority work and KV-cache warmups to proceed; 3) applies an eviction policy that drops the oldest/lowest-cost deferred requests when queue budget is exceeded; 4) provides a regional-safe fallback shim that, when a region trips a circuit threshold, automatically routes to a lightweight model variant and strips non-essential features (streaming and function-calls disabled, max_context truncated to 2k), reducing per-request resource pressure.

Design notes: the prioritizer is intentionally conservative: defer windows are short and there is a promotion path for requests which hit KV-cache warm state (we promote if prefix cache hit within the window). The fallback shim uses an explicit compatibility map: for each primary model there is a registered compact variant (e.g. redwood-instruct-large -> redwood-compact-psi). The decision logic is policy-driven (SLO-boundary checks, regional load, and feature flag gating).

Runtime flags and config: all behavior is feature-flagged under slo.deferred_prio_v2 and fallback.regional_safe_shim. Config knobs exposed in the console: defer_window_ms (default 250), deferred_queue_budget_tokens, promotion_threshold_ms (default 40), fallback_model_map, circuit_open_pct (default 85%).

Rollout plan: 1) merge behind flags; 2) canary 1% of traffic in a single low-risk region for 4 hours; 3) gradually ramp to 10% then 50% over 24 hours while monitoring error/latency signals; 4) auto rollback on increased request_error_rate > 0.5% absolute or P95 latency > SLO + 120ms for 3 consecutive eval windows (5m each). A canary job was added to perf-canary that runs synthetic traces with mixed priority distributions.

Observability: added the following metrics and traces: runtime.deferred_queue_depth, runtime.deferred_drop_rate, runtime.deferred_promotion_rate, fallback.routed_to_compact, fallback.feature_stripped_count. New dashboards: "Deferred Prioritizer" and a regional fallback heatmap. Alerts: deferred_drop_rate > 0.1% sustained for 5m triggers paging.

Testing: unit tests for prioritizer and eviction policy; integration tests that simulate KV warmups and promotion; perf lab runs showing p95 improvements under noisy neighbor scenarios. Also added an e2e smoke test for fallback shim routing behavior.

Risks and mitigations: risk of starvation for deferred requests — mitigated by an absolute latency cap and default conservative budget. Risk of quality regressions when routing to compact models — mitigated by explicit model map, consumer-facing release notes, and opt-out flags for customers with strict quality requirements.

Why different from previous load-shedding work: this is a behavioural scheduler that focuses on very short deferrals to let high-value in-flight work finish and warm caches, rather than broad shedding thresholds which immediately drop requests. The regional-safe fallback is a compatibility shim (model-feature downgrade) that keeps applications online with degraded feature set rather than failing entirely.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice approach. A few concerns on eviction ordering — can we make cost-weighting configurable?
Author (Asha): Made the cost-weighting a config param (deferred_queue_budget_tokens now respects per-request token_cost). Added unit tests to cover edge cases.
Noah Kim: Metrics look good. Please add a histogram for wait_time_in_deferred_queue to help tune default windows.
Author (Asha): Added wait_time histogram and updated dashboards in perf-canary. Also documented expected ranges in the runbook.
Priya Shah: QA found a race when promoting a request while the region trips a circuit. Can we make promotion atomic w.r.t. circuit evaluation?
Author (Asha): Fixed by moving promotion into the router's circuit-eval critical section and added an integration test that reproduces the race.
Noah Kim: LGTM. Verified perf numbers in the lab.
ci_checks: perf-bench: p95 under noisy neighbor scenario improved by 18%, throughput +7%
release_notes: Runtime: Add deferred SLO prioritizer and regional-safe fallback shim. Improves P95 latency under regional congestion by deferring low-priority requests and routing to compact model variants when a region trips a circuit. Behavior is behind feature flags (slo.deferred_prio_v2, fallback.regional_safe_shim). Admins can tune defer_window_ms and deferred_queue_budget_tokens in the Console.
notes_for_ops:
Canary instructions: use scripts/rollout/canary_deploy.sh --percent 1 --region us-west-2. Watch runtime.deferred_drop_rate and fallback.routed_to_compact. Rollback: toggle slo.deferred_prio_v2 off and run canary_deploy.sh to revert routing.
Alert thresholds in docs/ops/deferred-prioritizer-runbook.md.
